Detailed method

A slack round that needs a pot or a floured basket. Currently 500 g flour, 85% hydration, 20% starter, 2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 425 g water, 100 g starter, and 10 g salt, 1035 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 86.4% effective hydration. Currently 1 loaf of 1035 g. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 425 g water, the 100 g starter, and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 85% the dough is slack. Stop once the flour is wet. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Coil-fold it three times in the first 90 minutes. It is ready when it has grown by about half and jiggles.
  4. Shape Flour the top and set the 1035 g in a floured basket. Do not tighten it into a freestanding ball. This batch is 1 loaf. The default 1035 g uses a round lidded pot about 24 cm across and 11 cm high. If you change the amount, use a pot sized to fit, or split the dough.
  5. Proof Cover it for 45 to 75 minutes, until it looks puffy and a finger press springs back slowly. With 20% starter, bake it if the top starts to sink.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with the lidded pot inside. Place the dough on parchment and lower it, paper and all, into the hot pot. Score a spiral or a cross. Bake 20 minutes covered, then 18 to 24 minutes uncovered, until the crust is deep brown. If you have no lid, invert another pot or a deep tray over the loaf for the first 20 minutes. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
